subject: Clarification: RFP — SLA measurement methodology & crediting

Subject: Clarification: RFP — SLA measurement methodology & crediting

Hi Aditya / Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick response to the RFP. Attached is the SLA questionnaire from Aurelia's procurement and SRE teams (Aurelia_SLA_Questionnaire_20270910.xlsx). A few items we need clarification on before the legal/procurement team can accept your draft:

- Measurement source: Your draft states Redwood telemetry will be used as the primary data source. Aurelia's compliance requirement calls for customer-observed metrics to be the primary source for service credit calculations. Can Redwood support a reconciled (dual-source) approach?
- Aggregation window: Please confirm the aggregation window used to compute availability and latency (e.g., 1-min samples, 5-min rolling windows, 30-day rolling SLO).
- Credit calculation: Your current draft uses a per-incident credit; Aurelia favors an availability-based monthly credit calculation with a cap. Please provide a clear formula and an example calculation.
- Exclusions & maintenance: We need precise maintenance windows, blackout policies, and exclusions (e.g., DDoS, customer misconfig).

We're targeting a procurement decision by 2027-09-20; appreciate a response by EOD Monday 09/13 if possible.

Best,
Emma

Subject: Re: Clarification: RFP — SLA measurement methodology & crediting

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a focused SLA draft (Redwood_SLA_Draft_20270910.pdf) and a short diagram of our measurement pipeline (measurement-diagram.png). Below are concise answers and a proposed compromise we think meets Aurelia's controls while keeping crediting objective and actionable.

1) Measurement sources (proposed):
   - Primary: Redwood production telemetry (per-route request/response times, health checks, synthetic probes) aggregated by region.
   - Secondary (customer-observed): Aurelia-side metrics (ingested logs or APM traces) used for reconciliation and dispute resolution.
   - Reconciliation: Monthly reconciliation window; if customer-observed metrics consistently (>=3 consecutive days in a 30-day period) show >5% deviation from Redwood telemetry, both parties escalate to a joint verification with shared traces.

2) Aggregation & sampling:
   - Base sampling: 1-second buckets aggregated into 1-minute samples. Availability is computed per-minute.
   - Rolling SLO: 30-day rolling window for credit triggers; availability measured as proportion of healthy minutes in the window. Latency uses p99 over 5-minute aggregates sampled across regions.

3) Credit calculation (example):
   - Availability target: 99.95% in a 30-day rolling window.
   - If availability falls below target, credit = monthly invoice * min( (Target - Observed) / Target * 0.5, 0.25 ).
     - Example: Target 99.95%, Observed 99.50% -> Delta 0.45% -> Credit fraction = (0.45/99.95)*0.5 ≈ 0.00225 -> monthly credit ≈ 0.225% of invoice.
   - Max monthly credit cap: 25% of the invoice for platform outages attributable to Redwood.

4) Exclusions & maintenance:
   - Scheduled maintenance: Customers will be given a rolling 7-day notice for non-critical maintenance; scheduled maintenance windows (backwards compatible upgrades) excluded from availability calculations.
   - Force majeure / large-scale internet outages / DDoS events are excluded when they originate outside Redwood's control or when third-party providers declare an outage.
   - Customer misconfiguration (e.g., misrouted traffic, expired certs) excluded; however, misconfigurations that originated from Redwood-managed integrations are Redwood responsibility.

5) Probe methodology:
   - We run synthetic probes from six geographic vantage points (us-west, us-east, eu-west, eu-north, ap-south, ap-northeast) at 30s cadence. Probes exercise typical request patterns (small embedding, medium text generation, streamed chat first-token).
   - Probes are visible to customers via a shared dashboard; raw probe logs can be exported for joint analysis during disputes.

Next steps: Please confirm whether Aurelia requires customer-observed metrics to be the primary source (we've proposed Redwood telemetry primary + Aurelia reconciliation). If that is non-negotiable, we will propose a mirrored primary approach with a tight shared-trace escrow process.

Thanks — I can jump on a 30-minute call with your SRE lead today if helpful.

— Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Clarification: RFP — SLA measurement methodology & crediting

Emma / Aditya — a couple of practical clarifications from the product/SRE side I want on record before we finalize language:

- Reconciliation cadence: propose 7-day rolling checks for operational visibility and 30-day official reconciliation for credit calculations (so we have both fast detection and formal monthly accounting).
- Measurement anchor: define the endpoints included in the SLA explicitly (generation API endpoints, embeddings endpoint, and streaming first-token latency). That avoids ambiguity about background admin endpoints or non-customer-facing tools.
- Sampling bias: customer traffic patterns vary by payload size. We'll include a payload-size normalization clause for latency SLOs (p99 computed within normalized payload buckets: small, medium, large).
- Escalation path: include a technical three-step escalation (SRE sync within 24h, joint investigation within 72h, executive review within 10 business days) and a retention of raw traces for 90 days for dispute.

I've updated the draft to reflect the above and am attaching an internal redline for our legal team to review (see Redwood_SLA_Draft_20270910.pdf).

— Laura
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarification: RFP — SLA measurement methodology & crediting

Thanks Laura / Aditya — good detail. A couple of notes from Aurelia's SRE/legal teams after an internal review:

- Primary source: Aurelia's preference remains that customer-observed metrics be the primary determinant of crediting. If Redwood insists on Redwood telemetry as primary, Aurelia will require an automated cross-check service (daily reconciliation) and an agreed escrow of sampled traces for independent audit.
- Credit formula simplicity: procurement is pushing for a simpler tiered credit matrix rather than the continuous fractional formula (e.g., Availability < 99.9% = 5% credit, < 99.5% = 15%, < 98% = 25%). Could Redwood accept a tiered fallback in the contract and retain the continuous model for internal reporting?
- Measurement transparency: we need a per-region breakdown in monthly reports and retention of probe and production traces for 90 days (customer-accessible exports).

We are flexible on maintenance windows but will not accept more than 8 hours/month of scheduled, non-emergency maintenance without prorated credits. Please confirm if Redwood can cap scheduled maintenance to 8 hours/month in production regions supporting Aurelia.

If you can confirm these items today, our procurement/legal can incorporate changes and we will aim to circulate an initial redline by EOD 9/16.

Regards,
Emma
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Collins <emma.collins@aurelia.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: RFP — SLA measurement methodology & crediting

Emma — appreciate the constructive feedback. Summarizing agreed positions and concrete edits we'll include in the next redline by EOD 9/16: 

Agreed / committed items:
- Dual-source approach: Redwood telemetry remains our operational primary for rapid detection. Contract will state: customer-observed metrics can be designated as primary for credit calculations upon request; however, both sources will be reconciled via an automated daily cross-check with sampled trace escrow for independent review.
- Tiered credit fallback: We'll include the tiered credit matrix you proposed as an explicit contract fallback (5% / 15% / 25%) while preserving the continuous formula in an appendix for more granular internal accounting.
- Maintenance cap: Redwood will cap scheduled, non-emergency maintenance impacting production regions for Aurelia to 8 hours/month. Any overage will be pro-rated and treated as eligible for credits.
- Transparency & retention: Monthly per-region reports will be delivered and probe + production trace exports will be available for 90 days.
- Escalation & retention: We'll include the 3-step escalation (24h SRE sync, 72h joint investigation, 10 business-day executive review) and 90-day trace retention.

Open items for Aurelia to confirm (please reply):
- Do you want customer-observed metrics to be the automatic primary source, or to remain an opt-in contractual switch?
- Are you comfortable with the daily automated cross-check & sampled trace escrow approach?

Once you confirm, we'll finalize the redline and send to your procurement/legal. Happy to set a 30-min SRE call to demo our reconciliation logs and the probe dashboard.

Thanks — looking forward to closing.

— Aditya
